title: KernelBench-RL: Two Verified GPU Kernel Case Studies on an 8 GB Laptop

selection.scope: Selected successful case studies; not a complete held-out or model success rate.

paper.title: KernelBench-RL: Two Verified GPU Kernel Case Studies on an 8 GB Laptop
paper.abstract: This paper documents two selected positive examples of GPU kernel generation on an 8 GB laptop: fused bias plus GELU and matrix multiplication plus bias plus SiLU. Both saved programs were generated by a Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct adapter checkpoint and passed the recorded FP16 verification procedure. The paper explains each computation, the generated dataflow, correctness checks, and CUDA-graph timing boundaries. The result is 2/2 verified featured programs, selected after verification; it is not a complete-evaluation accuracy estimate. These case studies make no claim of incremental reinforcement-learning benefit or application-level acceleration.

environment.timing_scope: Steady-state per-invocation device latency from CUDA Graph replay; compilation, ordinary Python dispatch and end-to-end application latency are excluded.

cases.title: Bias + GELU
cases.summary: A bias addition and tanh-approximate GELU in one row-wise Triton kernel.
cases.application: A familiar activation pattern in transformer feed-forward layers. This case examines the operator itself, rather than a complete model.
cases.implementation: Each program loads a row and its bias, evaluates the tanh approximation using a sigmoid identity, and stores the FP16 result. Arithmetic uses FP32 intermediates.

evaluation.tolerance_note: FP16 worker acceptance uses atol=0.01 plus rtol=0.01 × reference magnitude; maximum absolute error alone is not the acceptance threshold.

cases.title: Matrix multiply + bias + SiLU
cases.summary: A tiled matrix product with its bias and SiLU epilogue inside the same kernel.
cases.application: Dense projections with an activation epilogue appear in neural-network execution. This example makes that fusion concrete at a fixed registered shape.
cases.implementation: The generated program uses 64 × 64 output tiles, a reduction block of 32, FP32 accumulation and a fused bias/SiLU epilogue before its FP16 store.

evaluation.tolerance_note: FP16 worker acceptance uses atol=0.01 plus rtol=0.01 × reference magnitude; maximum absolute error alone is not the acceptance threshold.
